sentences.text: Dzharatitanis is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Uzbekistan, containing only one known species, Dzharatitanis kingi.
The known fossil material consists of a single anterior tail vertebra, likely the first caudal vertebra.

The genus name Dzharatitanis combines the type locality Dzharakuduk with the suffix -titanis, referencing ancient Greek mythology, while the species name kingi honors the geologist Christopher King for his study of Central Asian Cretaceous rocks.
The holotype specimen USNM 538127 was discovered in 1997 by Hans-Dieter Sues and David J. Ward during an expedition to Uzbekistan, collected from the Bissekty Formation in the Navoiy Region.
Dzharatitanis kingi was formally described as a new genus and species in 2021 by Alexander Averianov and Hans-Dieter Sues.
Dzharatitanis is the first known rebbachisaurid from Asia and one of the last known members of the group.
While initially classified as a rebbachisaurid, later research suggests Dzharatitanis is a titanosaur and belongs to the parent group Somphospondyli.
Phylogenetic analysis places Dzharatitanis within the clade Lognkosauria, which includes giant titanosaurs like Patagotitan and Argentinosaurus.
Dzharatitanis lived during the Turonian age of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago, a timeframe that matches the span of its fossil record.
A study by Lerzo, Carballido, and Gallina disputed the rebbachisaurid classification, arguing instead that Dzharatitanis is a titanosaur.
